theorem_title: Existence of admissible approximation parameters for pi
natural_language_statement: For every real exponent ν > 2 and positive real constants Λ and c, assume arbitrarily large rational approximants exist: for every positive integer Q there are p ∈ ℤ and q ∈ ℕ with Q ≤ q and |π - p/q| ≤ q^(-ν). Then there exists an admissible configuration (as defined by the published admissible-parameter record), with the associated approximation, dimension and collision bounds, and positive uniform weight-error margins; it also carries a normalized sequence of successive approximations and a positive minimum weight.
explanation: The construction first selects published Parameters satisfying the hypothesis-dependent approximation bounds, then chooses an exponent gap ε, a large scale m, and a small rational σ. The proved dimension-margin and collision identities give the geometric bounds; the uniform weight-error, normalized successive-approximation, and minimum-weight results provide the remaining admissibility witnesses. The hypothesis is conditional: the statement does not assert that such approximants always exist.
